source.purpose: Final reference section for PSLE Science terminology, process skills, commonly tested terms and precise scientific wording. Use as supporting evidence for application marking and training-model generation. Do not silently overwrite the existing 89 memorisation sentences unless explicitly approved.

high_value_answering_rules.rule: For relationship questions, state how the measured variable changes as the changed variable increases or decreases. Name both variables explicitly.
high_value_answering_rules.example_pattern: As the changed variable increases, the measured variable increases/decreases.

high_value_answering_rules.rule: A hypothesis predicts how the changed variable affects the measured variable.
To increase reliability, repeat the experiment at least three times and calculate the average of the results. Reliable results are consistent/similar, not necessarily identical.
Accuracy means results are close to the actual/true value and is improved by suitable apparatus and careful procedure.
A control set-up is identical to the experimental set-up except for the changed variable. It allows comparison and helps confirm that the changed variable causes the measured effect.
For State questions, give a concise answer with little or no supporting explanation unless the question asks for it.

living_things: need air, food and water to survive

flower_reproduction.pollination: transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of the same flower or another flower of the same type/species
flower_reproduction.fertilisation: fusion of male and female reproductive cells

physical_science_precise_definitions.melting: change in state of a substance from solid to liquid at a fixed temperature due to heat gain
physical_science_precise_definitions.evaporation: change in state of a substance from liquid to gas at any temperature and takes place at the surface of the liquid
physical_science_precise_definitions.boiling: change in state of a substance from liquid to gas at a fixed temperature and takes place throughout the whole liquid
physical_science_precise_definitions.condensation: change in state of a substance from gas to liquid due to heat loss
physical_science_precise_definitions.freezing: change in state of a substance from liquid to solid at a fixed temperature due to heat loss
physical_science_precise_definitions.gaseous_exchange: taking in oxygen and removing carbon dioxide
physical_science_precise_definitions.respiration: breaking down glucose/sugar with the release of energy in living cells
physical_science_precise_definitions.photosynthesis: when a green plant takes in water and carbon dioxide in the presence of light trapped by chlorophyll to produce food/sugar/glucose and oxygen
physical_science_precise_definitions.gravitational_force: pull that acts on objects downwards towards the centre of Earth
physical_science_precise_definitions.elastic_spring_force: push or pull exerted by an object that is stretched or compressed
physical_science_precise_definitions.magnetic_force: force exerted by magnets on magnetic materials or other magnets
physical_science_precise_definitions.gravitational_potential_energy: energy possessed by an object above ground level
physical_science_precise_definitions.chemical_potential_energy: energy stored in food, fuel or a battery
physical_science_precise_definitions.elastic_potential_energy: energy possessed by an object that is stretched or compressed
physical_science_precise_definitions.kinetic_energy: energy possessed by moving objects; affected by mass and speed
physical_science_precise_definitions.mass: amount of matter in an object
physical_science_precise_definitions.volume: amount of space an object occupies
physical_science_precise_definitions.temperature: measure of the degree of hotness of an object
physical_science_precise_definitions.heat: a form of energy that causes the temperature of an object to change

experimental_process_skills.hypothesis: prediction of how the changed variable affects the measured variable
experimental_process_skills.relationship: how the measured variable changes with the changed variable
experimental_process_skills.fair_test: only one changed variable while other relevant variables are kept constant
experimental_process_skills.reliability: repeat experiment and look for consistent/similar results; calculate average when appropriate
experimental_process_skills.control_setup: same conditions except for the changed variable

time.stopwatch: measures time taken for an experiment

temperature.datalogger: measures temperature, including ranges beyond a normal thermometer depending on probe

volume.measuring_cylinder: measures volume of liquid with greater precision than a beaker
volume.beaker: measures approximate/moderate or large volumes of liquid
volume.syringe: measures small precise amounts of liquid
volume.conical_flask: contains/moderately measures liquid; commonly used in experiments
volume.funnel: pours liquid into a container with a small opening without spilling

support.retort_stand: clamps and holds objects in a fixed position

final_reference_notes: Weight is a force; mass is not a force.
Mass remains the same when location changes; weight can change when gravitational force changes.

Friction depends on type/roughness of surfaces and the force pressing surfaces together; in many school contexts heavier objects can experience greater friction because of greater normal contact force.
Like magnetic poles repel and unlike poles attract.
A magnet can attract magnetic materials even through some non-magnetic materials.
Heat flows from a hotter object/region to a cooler object/region until thermal conditions move toward equilibrium.
Temperature and heat are different: temperature measures hotness; heat is energy transfer/change related to temperature difference.
